description: Master URL routing, path converters, and creating views in Django

slides.title: Introduction to URLs and Views
slides.content:
# URLs and Views 🔗

Learn how Django routes requests to your code!

## What you'll learn:
- **URL routing** - How Django matches URLs
- **Creating views** - Function and class-based views
- **CBV & FBV** - When to use which
- **URL dispatcher** - The routing system
- **Path converters** - Dynamic URL parameters

## The Request Flow

```
User Request → URL Router → View → Response
     ↓              ↓         ↓        ↓
  /blog/5/      urls.py   views.py   HTML/JSON
```

## Why URL Design Matters

Clean URLs are:
- 👁️ **User-friendly** - Easy to read and remember
- 🔍 **SEO-friendly** - Search engines love them
- 🔧 **Maintainable** - Easy to update

```
✅ Good: /products/electronics/laptops/
❌ Bad:  /index.php?cat=5&subcat=12&type=3
```

> 💡 **Django's URL Philosophy:** URLs should be beautiful and permanent. Once published, they shouldn't change!

slides.title: URL Routing Basics
slides.content:
# URL Routing 📍

## How Django Finds the Right View

```
1. Request comes in: /blog/article/5/
2. Django loads ROOT_URLCONF (main urls.py)
3. Django tries each pattern in urlpatterns list
4. First match wins → calls the view
5. View returns response
```

## Basic URL Configuration

```python
# myproject/urls.py (main project)
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('blog/', include('blog.urls')),  # Include app URLs
    path('shop/', include('shop.urls')),
    path('', include('pages.urls')),      # Home pages
]
```

## App-Level URLs

```python
# blog/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.post_list, name='post_list'),
    path('create/', views.post_create, name='post_create'),
    path('<int:pk>/', views.post_detail, name='post_detail'),
]
```

## URL Resolution Order

```python
# Django tries patterns in order - first match wins!
urlpatterns = [
    path('about/', views.about),    # Checked first
    path('<slug:slug>/', views.page), # Checked second
]
# /about/ → about view (even though slug would match)
```

> ⚠️ **Order matters!** Put more specific patterns before general ones.

slides.title: Path Converters
slides.content:
# Path Converters 🔄

Capture values from URLs and pass them to views!

## Syntax

```python
path('<converter:name>/', views.my_view)
```

## Built-in Converters

| Converter | Matches | Example |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `str` | Any string (except `/`) | `hello-world` |
| `int` | Positive integers | `123` |
| `slug` | ASCII letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores | `my-post-title` |
| `uuid` | UUID format | `075194d3-6885-...` |
| `path` | Any string (including `/`) | `path/to/file` |

## Examples

```python
# blog/urls.py
urlpatterns = [
    # Integer ID
    path('article/<int:id>/', views.article_detail),
    # Matches: /article/5/, /article/123/
    
    # Slug for SEO-friendly URLs
    path('post/<slug:slug>/', views.post_detail),
    # Matches: /post/my-first-post/
    
    # Multiple converters
    path('archive/<int:year>/<int:month>/', views.archive),
    # Matches: /archive/2024/03/
    
    # UUID for unique identifiers
    path('order/<uuid:order_id>/', views.order_detail),
]
```

## Using Captured Values

```python
# views.py
def article_detail(request, id):
    # 'id' is automatically an integer!
    article = Article.objects.get(pk=id)
    return render(request, 'article.html', {'article': article})

def archive(request, year, month):
    # Both are integers
    posts = Post.objects.filter(date__year=year, date__month=month)
    return render(request, 'archive.html', {'posts': posts})
```

> 🎯 **Path converters validate and convert automatically!**

slides.title: Creating Views - FBV
slides.content:
# Function-Based Views (FBV) 📝

The simplest way to create views!

## Basic Structure

```python
from django.http import HttpResponse

def my_view(request):
    # request contains all info about the HTTP request
    # Must return an HttpResponse (or subclass)
    return HttpResponse("Hello, World!")
```

## View with Template

```python
from django.shortcuts import render

def article_list(request):
    articles = Article.objects.all()
    context = {
        'articles': articles,
        'title': 'All Articles'
    }
    return render(request, 'articles/list.html', context)
```

## Handling HTTP Methods

```python
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect

def contact(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        # Process form data
        name = request.POST.get('name')
        email = request.POST.get('email')
        message = request.POST.get('message')
        
        # Save to database or send email
        Contact.objects.create(name=name, email=email, message=message)
        
        return redirect('thank_you')
    
    # GET request - show form
    return render(request, 'contact.html')
```

## When to Use FBV

- ✅ Simple views with straightforward logic
- ✅ Quick prototyping
- ✅ Custom, unique logic
- ✅ When you need full control
- ✅ Learning Django (easier to understand)

> 💡 **FBVs are explicit and easy to follow - great for beginners!**

slides.title: Creating Views - CBV
slides.content:
# Class-Based Views (CBV) 🏗️

Powerful, reusable views using classes!

## Basic Class-Based View

```python
from django.views import View
from django.http import HttpResponse

class HomeView(View):
    def get(self, request):
        return HttpResponse("Welcome to our site!")
    
    def post(self, request):
        # Handle POST requests
        return HttpResponse("Data received!")
```

## URL Configuration for CBV

```python
# Note: Use .as_view() method!
from .views import HomeView

urlpatterns = [
    path('', HomeView.as_view(), name='home'),
]
```

## Adding Context Data

```python
from django.views.generic import TemplateView

class AboutView(TemplateView):
    template_name = 'about.html'
    
    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        context = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        context['team_members'] = User.objects.filter(is_staff=True)
        context['company_name'] = "My Company"
        return context
```

## When to Use CBV

- ✅ Standard CRUD operations
- ✅ Reusable, DRY code
- ✅ Complex views with mixins
- ✅ Following Django patterns
- ✅ Large projects with many similar views

> 🎯 **CBVs promote reusability through inheritance and mixins!**

slides.title: CBV vs FBV Comparison
slides.content:
# CBV vs FBV - When to Use Which? ⚖️

## Side-by-Side Comparison

```python
# Function-Based View
def article_list(request):
    articles = Article.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'articles/list.html', {'articles': articles})

# Class-Based View
class ArticleListView(ListView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/list.html'
    context_object_name = 'articles'
```

## Comparison Table

| Aspect | FBV | CBV |
|--------|-----|-----|
| **Simplicity** | ✅ Easy to understand | ❌ Steeper learning curve |
| **Reusability** | ❌ Less reusable | ✅ Highly reusable |
| **Flexibility** | ✅ Full control | ❌ May need overrides |
| **Code length** | ❌ More boilerplate | ✅ Less code for common patterns |
| **Debugging** | ✅ Easy to follow | ❌ Need to know parent classes |

## Decision Guide

```
Use FBV when:
├── Simple, unique logic
├── Learning Django
└── Full control needed

Use CBV when:
├── Standard CRUD operations
├── Reusing across views
└── Team consistency
```

> 💡 **Pro Tip:** Many developers start with FBV and refactor to CBV when patterns emerge. Both are valid!

slides.title: Generic Class-Based Views
slides.content:
# Generic Views 📦

Django provides built-in views for common patterns!

## Display Views

```python
from django.views.generic import ListView, DetailView, TemplateView

# Simple template rendering
class AboutView(TemplateView):
    template_name = 'about.html'

# List of objects
class ArticleListView(ListView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/list.html'
    context_object_name = 'articles'
    paginate_by = 10  # Built-in pagination!
    ordering = ['-created_at']

# Single object detail
class ArticleDetailView(DetailView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/detail.html'
    context_object_name = 'article'
```

## Editing Views

```python
from django.views.generic.edit import CreateView, UpdateView, DeleteView
from django.urls import reverse_lazy

class ArticleCreateView(CreateView):
    model = Article
    fields = ['title', 'content', 'category']
    template_name = 'articles/form.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('article_list')

class ArticleUpdateView(UpdateView):
    model = Article
    fields = ['title', 'content', 'category']
    template_name = 'articles/form.html'

class ArticleDeleteView(DeleteView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/confirm_delete.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('article_list')
```

> 💡 **Generic views handle forms, validation, and DB operations automatically!**

slides.title: URL Dispatcher Features
slides.content:
# URL Dispatcher 🎯 Advanced URL configuration features! ## Naming URLs ```python # Name your URLs for reverse resolution urlpatterns = [ path('', views.home, name='home'), path('article//', views.article_detail, name='article_detail'), path('article/create/', views.article_create, name='article_create'), ] ``` ## Using Named URLs in Templates ```html Read Article ❌ Read Article ✅ Home
``` ## Reverse in Views ```python from django.urls import reverse from django.shortcuts import redirect def my_view(request): # Get URL string url = reverse('article_detail', kwargs={'pk': 5}) # url = '/article/5/' # Redirect to named URL return redirect('article_list') # Or with arguments return redirect('article_detail', pk=5) ``` ## App Namespacing ```python # blog/urls.py app_name = 'blog' # Add namespace urlpatterns = [ path('', views.list, name='list'), ] # Usage in templates: {% url 'blog:list' %} # Usage in views: reverse('blog:list') ``` > 🎯 **Namespaces prevent conflicts between apps with same URL names!**

slides.title: Request and Response Objects
slides.content:
# Request & Response 📨 ## The Request Object ```python def my_view(request): # HTTP Method method = request.method # 'GET', 'POST', etc. # GET parameters (query string ?key=value) search = request.GET.get('search', '') page = request.GET.get('page', 1) # POST data (form submission) username = request.POST.get('username') password = request.POST.get('password') # User info user = request.user # Current user object is_authenticated = request.user.is_authenticated # Headers user_agent = request.headers.get('User-Agent') content_type = request.headers.get('Content-Type') # Path info path = request.path # '/blog/article/5/' full_path = request.get_full_path() # with query string # Other useful attributes request.is_ajax() # AJAX request? request.FILES # Uploaded files request.COOKIES # Cookies request.session # Session data ``` ## Response Types ```python from django.http import ( HttpResponse, JsonResponse, HttpResponseRedirect, Http404, ) # HTML response return HttpResponse("

Hello

") # JSON response (for APIs) return JsonResponse({'status': 'ok', 'data': [1, 2, 3]}) # Redirect return HttpResponseRedirect('/new-url/') # 404 error raise Http404("Page not found") # Shortcut for rendering templates return render(request, 'template.html', context) ```

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've mastered Django URLs and Views!

## URL Routing
- ✅ `urlpatterns` list in `urls.py`
- ✅ `path()` and `include()` functions
- ✅ App-level URL configuration
- ✅ Order matters - first match wins!

## Path Converters
- ✅ `int`, `str`, `slug`, `uuid`, `path`
- ✅ Automatic validation and conversion
- ✅ Multiple converters in one URL

## Creating Views (FBV)
- ✅ Simple functions that take `request`
- ✅ Return `HttpResponse` or use `render()`
- ✅ Handle GET/POST with `request.method`

## Class-Based Views (CBV)
- ✅ Use `.as_view()` in URL config
- ✅ Methods for each HTTP verb
- ✅ Generic views for common patterns

## URL Dispatcher
- ✅ Named URLs with `name='...'`
- ✅ `{% url %}` tag in templates
- ✅ `reverse()` in Python code
- ✅ App namespacing with `app_name`

## Request/Response
- ✅ `request.GET`, `request.POST`
- ✅ `JsonResponse` for APIs
- ✅ `render()` for templates

> 🚀 **Next Steps:** Learn about Templates to create beautiful HTML pages!
